Mathematics and Applications — Fundamental Mathematics

Université Paris-Saclay · France · Masters · Pure mathematics options

Dates not verified · window source reviewed 2026-10-12

Original name: Master Mathématiques et applications — parcours de recherche

M1 foundations lead toward specialized research M2 tracks; M1 and M2 are counted as one master pathway.

Tuition: Historical Funding: Historical Tests / supervisor: Verified Application dates: Not verified

Degree, admission, costs & funding
Length / structure
Two-year master pathway (M1 then M2); direct M2 admission is a separate entry stage, not an additional degree.
Teaching language
French / English varies
Academic preparation
Editorial preparation guide, not a formal admissions rule: proof-based linear algebra, real analysis, abstract algebra and topology. The official page governs degree equivalence and prerequisite credits.
Examination / supervisor
M1 applicants need an L3 fundamental-mathematics qualification or assessed equivalent; the dossier lists CV, motivation, identity and transcripts. The linked page gives 60 M1 places for this route, not university-wide admissions or a probability of acceptance.

Verified · Current programme requirements · reviewed 2026-10-12 · Source for this field

International applicants / process
Check whether your residence and qualifications require Mon Master, Études en France or the university’s M2 application portal. M1 and M2 have different entry requirements; do not submit through an assumed universal route.
Tuition
National public-master reference for 2026/27: EUR 255/year for EU/EEA/Swiss nationals and eligible equivalent-status categories; EUR 3,950/year differentiated tuition for liable non-EU students. University exemptions and their new conditions require an individual university decision; no blanket exemption is assumed. CVEC is separately EUR 105 for 2026/27 unless exempt. These are national prior-intake reference amounts, not a verified personal invoice or a published 2027/28 fee. Extra DU/school fees may apply.

Historical · National 2026/27 reference; individual exemptions unverified · reviewed 2026-10-12 · Source for this field

Funding
The 2026 international master scheme offers EUR 10,000/year (September–June) plus up to EUR 900/year travel/visa support. Applicants must be under 30 and generally first enrolling in France, admitted to an eligible Saclay master and selected by its coordinator. M1 renewal requires progression to an eligible M2; incompatible funding and reduced payments during some mobility/internships apply. The March 2026 selection/application deadlines are historical, not a verified 2027 call.

Historical · 2026 award call · reviewed 2026-10-12 · Source for this field

Intake / deadlines
The reviewed M1 page gives Inception applications January 15–March 16, 2026 for the 2026 course start. This is historical. The applicable 2027 M1/M2 portal and dates have not been published on that page; do not use the M2 AAG scholarship calendar for every M1 route.

Not verified · 2027 intake dates not established · reviewed 2026-10-12 · Source for this field

Published intake / admission statistics
The linked M1 page lists capacity 60 for its 2026 route. This is a programme capacity, not an acceptance rate or an admitted-student grade distribution.

The 2026/27 UGA IDEX call offers EUR 9,000 for M1 or EUR 5,500 for M2 for selected eligible international candidates. It is for one academic year; a second year requires a new competition. It does not waive tuition, not every programme awards it, and installments require enrollment/attendance/examinations. It is not an automatic award or a published 2027/28 package.

Tuition
2026–27 first instalment EUR 146 (EUR 130 regional tax + EUR 16 stamp); second instalment depends on ISEE, course area and progress. On-time/first-year-overrun students with ISEE ≤ EUR 30,000 owe no second instalment. New international students with foreign family finances use country/area rates: second instalment EUR 200–3,204 in area A or EUR 256–4,101.12 in area B, plus regional-tax adjustment. Mathematics area mapping remains unresolved.

Funding
Regional DSU 2026–27 applications ran 10 July–30 September 2026, including registered prospective students. First-year awards pay half initially; full payment depends on required merit, with revocation/repayment if not achieved by 30 November 2027. Separate university-funded scheme offers 1,055 awards of EUR 1,800 for applicants above the regional income ceiling. Full regional amount table, numeric eligibility and master's credit threshold remain access-blocked in linked notices.

First-year master's balance requires 20 credits by 10 August 2027; late achievement by 30 November halves award, otherwise repayment. Annual application, not guaranteed renewal.

Funding
MOE Tuition Grant is a subsidy, not a scholarship: eligible citizens receive it automatically; PR/international students apply and, if awarded/accepted, must work for a Singapore entity for three years after graduation. NUS International Undergraduate Scholarship: non-Singapore citizens applying as freshmen (not transfers), selected for academic/leadership/co-curricular merit; automatic consideration and shortlisted interviews. Covers subsidised tuition, SGD 5,800 living/year, SGD 5,000 accommodation/year, SGD 1,750 one-time computer grant; normal candidature, semester renewal at GPA >=3.5 and good conduct. No separate scholarship bond, but mandatory Tuition Grant creates the three-year obligation; concurrent awards need approval and early termination may trigger repayment. Science & Technology Scholarship separately includes Mathematics for Asian non-Singapore freshmen: subsidised tuition, SGD 6,000 living/year, SGD 1,750 computer and SGD 200 settling-in once, accommodation at lowest campus double-room rate and conditional travel allowance. Normal candidature; GPA >=3.5/good conduct each semester, SIX-year company bond, mandatory Tuition Grant, no concurrent funding and overseas-credit limits. Neither scheme guarantees an award or employment.
